cheatSheet.oneLineDefinition: Snowflake's Time Travel, Cloning, Streams, and Tasks provide native point-in-time recovery, storage-efficient environment copies, CDC change tracking, and automated SQL scheduling — enabling self-healing, event-driven ELT pipelines entirely within Snowflake.
keyConcepts: Time Travel: 1-day default (Standard), up to 90 days (Enterprise+); AT/BEFORE with TIMESTAMP/OFFSET/STATEMENT; UNDROP TABLE/SCHEMA/DATABASE
Fail-Safe: 7-day non-queryable Snowflake-managed recovery tier after Time Travel expires; not accessible via SQL
Zero-Copy Cloning: metadata pointer + copy-on-write; zero storage at creation; clones do NOT inherit masking/RAP policies
Streams: CDC object with internal offset; METADATA$ACTION (INSERT/DELETE), METADATA$ISUPDATE (boolean); offset advances on transaction COMMIT
Stream types: Standard (all DML), Append-Only (inserts only), Insert-Only (external/directory tables)
Tasks: single SQL or stored procedure; SCHEDULE = 'N MINUTE' or USING CRON; AFTER <parent> for DAGs; created in SUSPENDED state
Serverless Tasks: Snowflake manages compute; billed per second; no warehouse idle cost
SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA: boolean predicate for conditional task execution; skip task run when stream is empty
formulas: Stream staleness risk: stream goes stale if not consumed within DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS of the source table
Clone divergence cost = (new micro-partitions written to clone) + (new micro-partitions written to original after clone creation)
commands: CREATE DATABASE prod_clone CLONE prod AT(OFFSET => -3600);
CREATE STREAM my_stream ON TABLE my_source;
CREATE STREAM my_stream ON TABLE my_source APPEND_ONLY = TRUE;
SELECT * FROM my_stream WHERE METADATA$ACTION = 'DELETE' AND NOT METADATA$ISUPDATE;
CREATE TASK my_task WAREHOUSE = my_wh SCHEDULE = '5 MINUTE' WHEN SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA('my_stream') AS MERGE ...;
CREATE TASK child_task AFTER parent_task AS ...;
interviewPoints: Time Travel = user-queryable (AT/BEFORE SQL), 1–90 days; Fail-Safe = Snowflake-managed only, 7 days post-expiry, no SQL access
Zero-Copy Clone = metadata pointer at creation (zero cost); diverges via copy-on-write; does NOT inherit masking policies
UPDATE in a standard stream = DELETE row (old values, METADATA$ISUPDATE=TRUE) + INSERT row (new values, METADATA$ISUPDATE=TRUE)
Stream offset advances ONLY on successful transaction COMMIT of consuming DML — SELECT alone does not advance offset
Tasks are created SUSPENDED — always ALTER TASK RESUME after creation
SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA prevents empty task runs — skipped tasks appear as SKIPPED in TASK_HISTORY, not FAILED
Serverless tasks = no warehouse needed, auto-scaled, per-second billing — ideal for lightweight scheduled MERGE jobs
quickNotes: CREATE TRANSIENT TABLE skips Fail-Safe and limits Time Travel to 1 day — use for staging/temp tables to save storage costs
SHOW STREAMS has a STALE column — monitor this to catch streams that stopped being consumed before their retention window expired
Task DAG max depth is 5 levels in Snowflake; plan DAG architecture accordingly
EXECUTE TASK manually triggers a task immediately (ignores schedule) — useful for testing and backfill runs
AT(OFFSET) accepts negative seconds only (past); positive offsets are not valid
A cloned table inherits the source's current Time Travel history for shared micro-partitions but tracks new changes independently
Append-only streams cannot track UPDATE or DELETE operations — they will error if UPDATEs/DELETEs occur on append-only stream source tables that use that stream type

keyTakeaways: Time Travel and Fail-Safe are two distinct tiers: Time Travel (1–90 days, user-queryable via AT/BEFORE SQL) provides self-service point-in-time recovery and auditing, while Fail-Safe (always 7 days, non-queryable) is a Snowflake-managed last resort — users cannot access Fail-Safe data directly.

Zero-Copy Cloning costs nothing at creation because it writes only a metadata pointer to existing micro-partitions; additional storage is incurred only as the clone and original diverge through new DML (copy-on-write) — making it ideal for instant dev/test environment provisioning and pre-migration backups at any data scale.

Streams are passive CDC ledgers: they record DML changes but do not process them. The stream offset advances only when consuming DML (MERGE, INSERT SELECT) commits successfully inside a transaction — enabling safe automatic retry on failure without data loss or double-processing.

UPDATE operations on a standard stream surface as two rows (DELETE with old values + INSERT with new values, both with METADATA$ISUPDATE = TRUE) — failing to check METADATA$ISUPDATE in MERGE logic is the most common and silent stream-based data corruption bug.

Tasks are created in SUSPENDED state and must be explicitly resumed with ALTER TASK RESUME. Use WHEN SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA to skip task execution when no changes are pending, reducing unnecessary warehouse activations and compute costs.

Together, Streams + Tasks form a fully native Snowflake event-driven ELT pipeline that eliminates the need for external CDC connectors (Debezium) and schedulers (Airflow) for Snowflake-to-Snowflake incremental processing — reducing infrastructure complexity while providing built-in fault tolerance through transactional offset semantics.

Production maturity requires: setting DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS = 0 on transient staging tables, explicitly applying masking policies after cloning, monitoring stream staleness daily, alerting on task FAILED states via TASK_HISTORY, and using serverless tasks for lightweight scheduled jobs to eliminate idle compute costs.
